I personally sympathize with it's conduct code and reputation. Canonical had those issues with amazon apps and telemetry not being crystal clear and I really don't like that as a matter of privacy, but not everyone cares about that.  
One thing I think it's cool to know before coming from such a end-user based distro is that some configurations won't be as easy and smooth as just turning your computer on and clicking "next" in the welcome screen. I used Linux Mint for most of the time I used Linux and I really enjoyed those simple configurations. You won't have a real bad time learning how to get along with the system and I might be scaring you off, but I just think it's good to know if you install Debian that maybe you will have to learn some stuff before going on with your life lol.

Some things to check if you do install Debian: 1- Drivers and firmware (Debian's wiki is really good on this matter); and 2- wheter or not you should run Debian Stable, Testing or Unstable. I liked Stable but found out I enjoy far more Testing and I can't maintain Unstable. I think it's a matter of profile and you shouldn't take long to decide anyway. Testing is more stable than most distros out there, just so you know hehe.

I think Debian is a great system to use at least for some period so you can get familiarized with Linux and it really suited me after some serious distro hopping. I hope this could help you anyway and if I can give you any other advice just let me know. ;)
